subject: why I got same chi-square, P value for different data using the same full model structure?

messages.author: c72a7040a2ed8cad
messages.subject: why I got same chi-square, P value for different data using the same full model structure?
parts:
Hi all,

Due to my limited knowledge, I am a bit confused about the results from my study.
I did an experiment, including three factors (A, B and C). My measurements include one mediator (M) and other two variable (X, Y).

In my full model:

M ~ A + B + C
X ~ A + B + C + M
A ~~ 0*B
A ~~ 0*C
B ~~ 0*C

I sent no correlation between three factors, due to the design of my experiment.

I found that the chi-square and P value in the test (use ML) for X are the same as them in the text for Y.

I don't understand why...

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: why I got same chi-square, P value for different data using the same full model structure?
parts:
The rest of your model is saturated.  All bivariate relationships are freely estimated between X (or Y) and M, and each of those with A, B, and C.  The only part of the model that gives you degrees of freedom is fixing the A-B-C correlation matrix to zero, but that is the same in both models.  Because all other relationships in the saturated part of the model will be perfectly reproduced (and the sample sizes of observed data in X and Y are the same), the only source of misfit in the model for X (or for Y) is from fixing the A-B-C correlations to zero, so the fit statistic (and its p value) will be the same.

Terry
